note: The OLG's Self-Employment SNAP page thoroughly covers all four SE income budgeting scenarios from FNS 1065.1: (1) Annual SE income earned in a shorter period must be averaged over 12 months — covered in 'Averaging Self-Employment Income' section; (2) Fluctuating SE income must be averaged — covered via the anticipating/averaging guidance; (3) SE income for only part of the year must be prorated — explicitly covered in the summer vendor example ('must have their self-employment income averaged over the summer months rather than a 12-month period'); (4) Steady SE income needs no annualizing — covered in 'Anticipating Self-Employment Income' section for non-averaged SE income. The FNS 'Reported Source' and 'Unreported Source' subsections describe QC reviewer correction procedures (correcting EW errors, calculating AORD figures for unreported income) — these are QC methodology, not caseworker policy, and do not require OLG coverage. The FNS section itself notes 'States have flexibility in their definition and treatment of SE income,' and the OLG provides comprehensive, worker-actionable guidance on all policy-relevant aspects.
